subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the adjoint and the inverse of the matrix with rows (cos α, −sin α) and (sin α, cos α).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.102 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 152. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed VSAQ on its length and shape — the adjoint and inverse of a 2×2 is exactly Unit 3's VSAQ answers 111.x. The bank heading on this page reads only "MATRICES", so the section is OURS. Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. A rotation matrix. Its determinant is exactly 1 because cos²α + sin²α = 1 — which is why its inverse is simply its adjoint, and also its transpose. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular 1x7 for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find |A| and the adjoint
steps.margin_note: First mark. The 2×2 shortcut: swap the diagonal, flip the signs of the other two. The determinant comes out as the Pythagorean identity.
steps.memory_tip: The 2×2 shortcut: swap the diagonal, flip the signs of the other two. The determinant is the Pythagorean identity.

recall.must_convey: That |A| = cos²α + sin²α = 1, and the adjoint swaps the diagonal and negates the other two entries.
accept: the determinant is cos squared plus sin squared which is one and the adjoint swaps the diagonal and flips the other signs
use the two by two shortcut for the adjoint
the determinant comes to one by the Pythagorean identity
determinant one, adjoint ki diagonal swap chesi signs marchali
find the determinant and the adjoint

steps.why: A determinant of exactly 1 means the matrix preserves area — which is what a rotation does. The geometry and the algebra agree here.
common_mistakes: Getting the determinant as cos²α − sin²α.
Negating the diagonal instead of the off-diagonal.

steps.label: Divide by |A|
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Dividing by 1 changes nothing, so the inverse IS the adjoint — and it is also A transposed, which is worth noticing.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing by 1 changes nothing, so the inverse IS the adjoint — and it is also A transposed.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by |A| = 1 leaves the adjoint unchanged, so A⁻¹ equals the adjoint — and equals Aᵀ.
accept: the determinant is one so the inverse is just the adjoint, which is also A transpose
the inverse equals the transpose here
determinant one kabatti inverse adjoint ye, adi A transpose kuda

steps.why: A matrix whose inverse is its transpose is called orthogonal — and every rotation matrix is one. That is the general fact behind this particular answer.
common_mistakes: Writing the division line as if it changed something.
Missing that the answer is also Aᵀ.
